CVE-2026-48978 (GHSA-xf85-363p-868w, GO-2026-5885): the oras-go registry authentication client followed the realm URL from a registry's WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge without validating its scheme or host, so a malicious or compromised registry, or a man-in-the-middle on a plaintext connection, could make the client send requests carrying the user's credentials to internal addresses such as a cloud instance metadata endpoint, or move the token request from https to plain http. It affects oras.land/oras-go/v2 before 2.6.1, in the auth Client.Do function (package registry/remote/auth), and is fixed in 2.6.1 by commit 7a9f4b0b (https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/commit/7a9f4b0b9558821b0422152ebe21ae56930fe764). The fix adds a realm check (validateRealm in registry/remote/auth/client.go) that rejects realms with a scheme other than http or https, http realms for a registry reached over https, and realm hosts that are loopback, link-local, private or unspecified IP addresses unless the registry itself was reached at that same host. Cross-host realms on public hostnames remain allowed by design: the advisory's 'What is NOT claimed' section says forwarding credentials to a public host named by a registry's realm is not, on its own, the vulnerability. GitHub's advisory lists v2.6.2 as the first patched release; the fix commit is in v2.6.1 and every later release. Sources: https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/security/advisories/GHSA-xf85-363p-868w, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5885 and https://github.com/oras-project/oras-go/releases/tag/v2.6.1. We checked every scout-sbom-indexer-dev package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository as of 28 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-r1 to the current 1.30.0-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64 (50 packages), each against the checksum in the repository index. Each package holds one file, /sbom-indexer, a statically linked Go program for Linux built with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). We read the program in full from every package, except 1.26.0-r3, whose program has the same SHA-1 checksum, recorded in its package header, as the 1.26.0-r2 program we read. The -dev program is built without the -w linker flag and without -trimpath; its Go release and module versions are the same as those of the scout-sbom-indexer program of the same build. Its Go build information, the same on both architectures, lists oras.land/oras-go/v2 v2.6.0 in 1.20.4-r1 to 1.23.1-r0, v2.6.2 in 1.23.1-r1 to 1.30.0-r0, with no replace directive for that module. Reading the program's Go function table in every build (runtime.main found in every build as a control) shows the vulnerable function, oras.land/oras-go/v2/registry/remote/auth.(*Client).Do, linked in every build. The builds before 1.23.1-r1 carry v2.6.0, before the fixed 2.6.1, and every build from 1.23.1-r1 on carries v2.6.2, which contains the fix commit (no build carries 2.6.1), so 1.23.1-r1 is the first fixed build.
